summary: Jean's Head light at New Perlican, Trinity Bay: an octagonal wooden tower lit in 1915, a skeletal tower today, a municipal heritage site since 2013.

structures.note: Octagonal wooden lighthouse joined to a one-storey keeper's dwelling by a covered passageway. Lighthouse Friends gives 27 ft. Standing through at least 1958 (Light Lists, per Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett says at least through the late 1950s).
Square skeletal tower with a red-and-white daymark, showing a flashing white light by 2021 (Lighthouse Friends). Coast Guard list gives the height above ground as 4.3 m; Rowlett gives 4.5 m (15 ft).

access.note: Reached on foot by a walking trail from New Perlican. The town maintains the hiking trail to the point (Rowlett). The former station grounds are part of a hiking trail system (heritage statement).

events.note: Put into operation September 1915, per the notice to mariners quoted in the heritage statement. Light: white, occulting, 7 s shown and 3 s eclipse; 48.6 m above high water.
Octagonal wooden lighthouse and one-storey keeper's dwelling joined by a covered passageway.
Light automated; characteristic changed to a flashing white light with a two-second period (Lighthouse Friends). The Coast Guard list now gives Fl W 4s.
Municipal heritage site, Town of New Perlican, Council motion 2013-062, 13 July 2013.
Square skeletal tower showing a flashing white light by 2021; the year it replaced the wooden tower is not given.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The heritage statement says the light station no longer stands, yet the same statement describes a square skeleton tower carrying a light on the site. Lighthouse Friends describes that tower by 2021, and the Coast Guard list shows the light active. The story treats the light as in service and the 1915 wooden lighthouse as gone.
Jean's Head and Jane's Head are both in use. The heritage statement says government records used Jean's Head at establishment.
Lighthouse Friends gives a flashing white light with a two-second period from 1931. The Coast Guard list gives Fl W 4s today. The story gives both, with their dates.

Lighthouse Friends gives 27 ft (8.2 m) for the 1915 wooden tower. For the present skeletal tower the Coast Guard list gives 4.3 m above ground and Rowlett gives 4.5 m (15 ft). The story gives both present-tower figures with their sources.

notes_for_editor: Thin record with five sources; three are secondary (heritage statement, Lighthouse Friends, Rowlett). No primary text was read for the 1915 notice to mariners, the 1890 newspaper pieces, or the keepers' appointments. The Year Book and Almanac of Newfoundland 1915 (archive.org) has a table of lights listing 'Jean's Head, Trinity Bay' with a position near the Coast Guard's; its status column is printed as a separate OCR block, so it is not footnoted. Newfoundland was outside Canada before 1949, so the Canadian Department of Marine reports in the corpus do not cover this light. Coast Guard position 47 55 37.3 N, 53 21 48.5 W agrees with the record location within about 0.01 degree. Status conflict (heritage 'no longer stands' against the skeletal tower and the Coast Guard list) is stated in the story. Ownership of the present tower is not given by any source read; the record's 'unknown' stands. Keeper roster is from Lighthouse Friends and the heritage statement only; no post-1931 keepers are known. Web searches: 3. Page reads: about 11. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the present tower's height is now given from the Coast Guard list (4.3 m above ground) beside Rowlett's 4.5 m. The owner of the present tower is still not given by any source read.
